1: # Plan — Master Index & Doc Architecture
2: 
3: This document defines **how this planning set is structured** and how it will be executed. It is the entry point for any human or agent reading this repo.
4: 
5: ## Project
6: 
7: - **Name:** `noAir` (GitHub repo `noair-movie-downloader`)
8: - **One-line purpose:** Self-hosted web app that searches movies/TV via TMDB, finds torrent/magnet sources via Prowlarr, downloads them with qBittorrent (Docker), shows live download progress, and plays the finished video in-browser (or hands it to the user's local player).
9: 
10: ## Goal of this doc set
11: 
12: Produce a complete, unambiguous blueprint so that:
13: 
14: - A human can review the entire plan in under 15 minutes.
15: - An agent can execute the whole build top-to-bottom **without making design decisions**.
16: - Every task has a verifiable "done" condition.
17: 
18: ## Doc layout
19: 
20: ```
21: AGENTS.md                        # Project rules, commands, conventions — always read first
22: docs/plan/
23:   00-index.md                    # THIS FILE — overview, build order, locked decisions
24:   01-architecture.md             # System design: components, data flow, boundaries
25:   02-specs.md                    # Concrete contracts: API, data model, UI, providers
26:   03-tasks.md                    # Ordered, numbered milestones w/ acceptance criteria
27: ```
28: 
29: ## What each doc is FOR (and what it is NOT for)
30: 
31: | File | Contains | Must NOT contain |
32: |------|----------|------------------|
33: | `AGENTS.md` | Repo-level rules, run commands, edit conventions, pointer to this index | Project design decisions |
34: | `00-index.md` | Scope, goals, **locked decisions**, build order, conventions for the docs themselves | Implementation detail |
35: | `01-architecture.md` | Components, responsibilities, data flow diagrams, tech boundaries, what talks to what | Line-by-line implementation |
36: | `02-specs.md` | Concrete contracts: endpoints + payloads, schema, UI screens/flows, provider interfaces | Rationale, alternatives, opinions |
37: | `03-tasks.md` | Numbered tasks in build order; each with inputs, outputs, acceptance criteria | Design discussion |
38: 
39: ## Rules for writing every doc
40: 
41: 1. **Decisions, not options.** Every "we could use X or Y" becomes "we use X." No open choices left for the executor.
42: 2. **Requirements + acceptance criteria, not prose.** Facts an agent can verify. No ambiguous adjectives.
43: 3. **One fact lives in one place.** If two docs disagree, the doc that "owns" it wins (ownership table below). Cross-reference instead of duplicating.
44: 4. **Precise naming.** All names are written exactly once in `02-specs.md` and reused verbatim everywhere else.
45: 5. **No "later"/"TBD" in a doc that the executor reads.** Anything unknown is recorded in this file under Open Questions, resolved, then moved into the relevant doc.
46: 
47: ## Ownership table (single source of truth)
48: 
49: | Topic | Owned by |
50: |-------|----------|
51: | Tech stack, scope, build order | `00-index.md` |
52: | Components and data flow | `01-architecture.md` |
53: | API contracts, data model, UI, provider behavior | `02-specs.md` |
54: | Milestones, task order, acceptance criteria | `03-tasks.md` |
55: 
56: ## Locked decisions
57: 
58: | # | Decision |
59: |---|----------|
60: | D1 | Backend: **Node.js + Express 4 + TypeScript**. Single-user app, no auth. |
61: | D2 | Frontend: **React 18 + Vite + TypeScript**, React Router, **Zustand** for client state, plain CSS (no UI framework). |
62: | D3 | Database: **PostgreSQL 16 as a Docker service** (named volume), `pg` driver, schema run on backend boot. |
63: | D4 | Torrent indexer: **Prowlarr (Docker)**. One normalized search API; trackers (TPB, 1337x, etc.) configured in Prowlarr, not in code. |
64: | D5 | Downloader: **qBittorrent (Docker)** via its Web API v2. Backend polls it every 2s. |
65: | D6 | Metadata + imagery: **TMDB API** (free key). All poster/backdrop images proxied by the backend so the key never reaches the browser. |
66: | D7 | Realtime UI updates: **Socket.IO**. Server pushes a full downloads snapshot every 2s. |
67: | D8 | Playback: **play only after the file is fully downloaded**. qBittorrent writes in-progress files as `x.mkv.!qb` and renames them when complete; the backend never lists or serves `.!qb` files, so `stream_file_path`/`streamable` appear only once a complete file exists (inside a season pack, individually-completed episodes unlock early). Completed files are served over HTTP **Range** (`/api/stream/:infoHash`) for external players and browser-safe direct playback; `lib/streamPlan.ts` still routes browser-unsupported audio (→ AAC remux) and sub-4K HEVC (→ H.264 transcode) through ffmpeg for *completed* files, and 4K/UHD non-safe video to the external-player flow via the `movie://` scheme. Browser codec limits (H.264/VP9/AV1; no HEVC/.avi guarantee) still apply. `playinfo` also probes every audio/subtitle track for the browser-player upgrade. Packaging never re-encodes browser-safe AAC-LC audio (stream-copied) and runs renditions concurrently (S14); before packaging, Watch probes `mseProbe` codec strings and routes undecodable video (e.g. HEVC Main10) straight to the external-player screen. |
68: | D9 | Deployment: single `docker-compose.yml` with services `postgres`, `qbittorrent`, `prowlarr`, `backend`, `frontend`. Frontend served by nginx that proxies `/api` and `/socket.io` to the backend. |
69: | D10 | Cost: everything is free/open-source. Only required external account is a free TMDB API key; an **optional free OMDb key** (`OMDB_API_KEY`) enables portrait posters for the wide tiles (§4.6) — cards degrade to monograms when absent. |
70: | D11 | Testing: **Vitest** on the backend (unit tests with mocked providers); frontend smoke test via manual run in M4. |
71: | D12 | Magnet links: prefer Prowlarr-provided magnet; otherwise build from `infoHash` + 9 public trackers (list in `02-specs.md` §4.3). |
72: | D13 | LAN exposure: `frontend`, `qbittorrent` (Web UI), and `prowlarr` are all published on host ports (`0.0.0.0`). qBittorrent must have strong credentials (it has its own login); Prowlarr has no auth — documented risk accepted for a home LAN. `postgres` and `backend` stay internal-only. |
73: | D14 | TV browsing (v2): TV titles present TMDB **seasons/episodes**; contextual Prowlarr searches are whole-show (S3 no params), per-season (`?season=N` → season packs + episode releases), or per-episode (`?season=N&episode=M`). The Advanced picker retains the 30-row "Load more" + client-side filters/grouping from v1. **Friendly downloads auto-pick the most-seeded matching source**; releases with unparseable coverage are Advanced-only; a per-episode download never silently pulls a whole season. |
74: | D15 | Frontend visual language: **Netflix-style; black & white UI chrome over full-color artwork**. Left sidebar removed; fixed top header transparent at top that fades to a black gradient on scroll. Home = static cinematic brand hero + **16:9 full-bleed title-card tiles** (whole-card click, no captions/info icons) that bleed full-width with the rightmost card clipped to invite scroll; full-screen search overlay. Card art (superseded clause → **D21**): every tile is now the **OMDb-portrait composite** (no FanArt/TMDB imagery). Rail named "My Downloads"; **local-only playback resume** (C-DL2); **every friendly download opens a confirm sheet** naming the exact pick (C-DL1); **inline first-run guidance** (C-DL3). |
75: | D16 | TV metadata + episode columns: new `GET /api/media/:id/season/:n` (S12); `Source.coverage` from release titles with season gating on S3; downloads gain nullable `season_number`/`episode_number`/`backdrop_path` via idempotent `ALTER TABLE`; the file-list endpoint (S13) tags each file with season/episode server-side; `/watch/:infoHash?episode=SxxExx` auto-selects the matching file inside a season pack; the poll backfills season on legacy TV rows. |
76: | D17 | **~~Artwork pipeline v2 (poster-first tiles)~~ — SUPERSEDED by D21.** Kept for history: card identity is the poster, not the backdrop (Fanart/TMDB ladder, `art_files` cache, temporary `cardStyle` A/B). All of it (FanArt provider, enrichment, the Settings artwork controls) is **removed** by D21; only the `art_files` "poster on disk served via S8b" mechanism survived, re-sourced to OMDb. |
77: | D18 | **Hover-trailer previews — data layer**: every `TitleCard` resolves the title's best trailer for the hover card. Trailer metadata comes from TMDB `GET /movie/{id}/videos` / `GET /tv/{id}/videos` through the existing key — **no new key, no YouTube Data API, no backend storage** (`S15`). TV cards use the **series** trailer (per-episode trailers are not surfaced — TMDB coverage is sparse). The on-card presentation is **D20** (this entry no longer defines rendering). Embedding requires the *browser* to reach YouTube/Vimeo; the LAN box only needs TMDB reachability. |
78: | D19 | **Movie "the download is the loading screen" + version grouping**: the movie Detail hero renders one primary state (`DownloadsHeroPanel`) — no copy → Download best-match (inline "Best match · quality · size · seeds" hint, **Advanced**; shimmer while resolving) · copies arriving → status card (big tabular %, state, speed·ETA, Pause/Resume, Remove) · something playable → exactly one ▶ **Watch** (active version) + Player + delete with a **version-chip row** to switch, copies still downloading folded into mini-rows; **a disabled Watch is never rendered**. Best-source search runs only when the title owns no copy, is deduped + cached in the API client per context (~10 min), and lazily re-fetches after the last copy is deleted. Releases of one movie are **versions of a single library item** (`lib/versions.ts` pure helpers + `store/versionStore` persisted to `localStorage` keyed `movie:<tmdbId>`; default rule = most recently completed playable copy, tie-break higher resolution): My Downloads shows one card per movie with hover version chips; the Downloads page groups copies under `Movie · N versions` headers and labels each row `audio · quality`. Downloads persist `audioLang`/`audioMode` (idempotent `ALTER`, `S4`) so copies differing only by language stay distinguishable. TV keeps its episode layout and only reuses the panel for the active season pack; the C-DL1 confirm sheet is unchanged. |
79: | D20 | **Expanded Netflix-style hover card (replaces D18's inline overlay)**: every `TitleCard` expands into a **portaled, fixed pop-up card** after a sustained ~600 ms hover — width **1.7×** the base card (viewport-clamped), **vertically centered on the base cell (grows equally above and below)** and horizontally centered so it **overflows the neighbouring cards on all four sides**, `z-index: 150`, 8 px radius + strong dark shadow; base card keeps its grid slot (no white ring/scale while open); any scroll/resize dismisses it. Split layout: **media top (16:9)** = autoplay-looped trailer with **sound ON by default** (Chrome silences unmuted autoplay until the user has clicked the app once) + circular mute/unmute button that **remounts the iframe** (clip restarts), title/logo bottom-left over a scrim; **details bottom (dark column)** = compact Netflix-matching panel (16 px gutters, ~1.35 line-height, medium-500 13 px text): row 1 = Play (white circle → primary Watch action when present, else Detail) + two **decorative no-op circles** (Add to List `+`, Rate thumbs-up) + More Info chevron; My-Downloads version chips sit on their **own row beneath the actions**; row 2 = monochrome age-badge (`certification`) · duration ("2h 15m") or season count ("N Seasons") · `HD` chip (all 1 px translucent outlines, ~11 px); row 3 = up to three genre tags joined by `•`. Typeface is self-hosted **Inter Variable** (proprietary **Netflix Sans** is never bundled) standing in for the Netflix look. Data arrives from **S16** (`GET /api/media/:id/hover`), one call returning trailer + genres + runtime + seasons + certification, cached client-side ~1 h; US rating comes from TMDB `release_dates`/`content_ratings`. Every card expands even with no trailer (still artwork stands in); no pop-up for reduced-motion, `tmdbId <= 0`, or a failed/failed payload (static card). |
80: | D21 | **Netflix-style wide tiles from OMDb portraits — the winning card-art source.** Research: no free API serves *wide* per-title studio art except TMDB backdrops/FanArt (Netflix title cards are proprietary; OMDb returns only a portrait `Poster`). Decision: **wide 16:9 tile composited in-app from the OMDb portrait** — crisp portrait figure at full tile height over its own blurred ground; used everywhere (rails, My Downloads, downloads page, search, Detail hero as blurred ground). Pipeline: TMDB external_ids `imdbId` → OMDb (`OMDB_API_KEY`, budgeted ~850 req/day) → Amazon portrait downloaded once to the `art` volume (`art_files`, kind `poster`) → served by S8b, which **warms on first miss**; `empty` rows cached 7 days; no poster → monogram (never TMDB/FanArt imagery). **FanArt.tv and the whole artwork-settings cluster are deleted** (provider toggle, per-size preference, `cardStyle` A/B, preview tester, `ART_GRID` spike, `FANART_API_KEY`, `media_art`); `/api/settings` is audio-only; Settings shows no artwork controls. S8 TMDB proxy remains only for TV episode stills. |

82: ## Build order (how 03-tasks.md is sequenced)
83: 
84: Every milestone must be independently runnable and verifiable before the next starts:
85: 
86: 1. Project scaffold (repo layout, tooling, config, docker-compose, CI if any).
87: 2. Core domain logic that has no external dependencies (unit-testable first).
88: 3. External integrations one at a time, each behind an interface (TMDB, Prowlarr, qBittorrent).
89: 4. API layer over the domain logic (REST + Socket.IO).
90: 5. UI layer.
91: 6. End-to-end wiring, polish, and verification.
92: 
93: ## Execution protocol
94: 
95: 1. Agent reads `AGENTS.md`, then this file, then `03-tasks.md`.
96: 2. Agent works through tasks **in order**. Each task names exactly which of the other docs to read.
97: 3. After each task, the agent reports what it did and how the acceptance criteria were verified.
98: 4. A human confirms each milestone before the next begins.

# Plan — Master Index & Doc Architecture

This document defines **how this planning set is structured** and how it will be executed. It is the entry point for any human or agent reading this repo.

## Project

- **Name:** `noAir` (GitHub repo `noair-movie-downloader`)
- **One-line purpose:** Self-hosted web app that searches movies/TV via TMDB, finds torrent/magnet sources via Prowlarr, downloads them with qBittorrent (Docker), shows live download progress, and plays the finished video in-browser (or hands it to the user's local player).

## Goal of this doc set

Produce a complete, unambiguous blueprint so that:

- A human can review the entire plan in under 15 minutes.
- An agent can execute the whole build top-to-bottom **without making design decisions**.
- Every task has a verifiable "done" condition.

## Doc layout

```
AGENTS.md                        # Project rules, commands, conventions — always read first
docs/plan/
  00-index.md                    # THIS FILE — overview, build order, locked decisions
  01-architecture.md             # System design: components, data flow, boundaries
  02-specs.md                    # Concrete contracts: API, data model, UI, providers
  03-tasks.md                    # Ordered, numbered milestones w/ acceptance criteria
```

## What each doc is FOR (and what it is NOT for)

| File | Contains | Must NOT contain |
|------|----------|------------------|
| `AGENTS.md` | Repo-level rules, run commands, edit conventions, pointer to this index | Project design decisions |
| `00-index.md` | Scope, goals, **locked decisions**, build order, conventions for the docs themselves | Implementation detail |
| `01-architecture.md` | Components, responsibilities, data flow diagrams, tech boundaries, what talks to what | Line-by-line implementation |
| `02-specs.md` | Concrete contracts: endpoints + payloads, schema, UI screens/flows, provider interfaces | Rationale, alternatives, opinions |
| `03-tasks.md` | Numbered tasks in build order; each with inputs, outputs, acceptance criteria | Design discussion |

## Rules for writing every doc

1. **Decisions, not options.** Every "we could use X or Y" becomes "we use X." No open choices left for the executor.
2. **Requirements + acceptance criteria, not prose.** Facts an agent can verify. No ambiguous adjectives.
3. **One fact lives in one place.** If two docs disagree, the doc that "owns" it wins (ownership table below). Cross-reference instead of duplicating.
4. **Precise naming.** All names are written exactly once in `02-specs.md` and reused verbatim everywhere else.
5. **No "later"/"TBD" in a doc that the executor reads.** Anything unknown is recorded in this file under Open Questions, resolved, then moved into the relevant doc.

## Ownership table (single source of truth)

| Topic | Owned by |
|-------|----------|
| Tech stack, scope, build order | `00-index.md` |
| Components and data flow | `01-architecture.md` |
| API contracts, data model, UI, provider behavior | `02-specs.md` |
| Milestones, task order, acceptance criteria | `03-tasks.md` |

## Locked decisions

| # | Decision |
|---|----------|
| D1 | Backend: **Node.js + Express 4 + TypeScript**. Single-user app, no auth. |
| D2 | Frontend: **React 18 + Vite + TypeScript**, React Router, **Zustand** for client state, plain CSS (no UI framework). |
| D3 | Database: **PostgreSQL 16 as a Docker service** (named volume), `pg` driver, schema run on backend boot. |
| D4 | Torrent indexer: **Prowlarr (Docker)**. One normalized search API; trackers (TPB, 1337x, etc.) configured in Prowlarr, not in code. |
| D5 | Downloader: **qBittorrent (Docker)** via its Web API v2. Backend polls it every 2s. |
| D6 | Metadata + imagery: **TMDB API** (free key). All poster/backdrop images proxied by the backend so the key never reaches the browser. |
| D7 | Realtime UI updates: **Socket.IO**. Server pushes a full downloads snapshot every 2s. |
| D8 | Playback: **play only after the file is fully downloaded**. qBittorrent writes in-progress files as `x.mkv.!qb` and renames them when complete; the backend never lists or serves `.!qb` files, so `stream_file_path`/`streamable` appear only once a complete file exists (inside a season pack, individually-completed episodes unlock early). Completed files are served over HTTP **Range** (`/api/stream/:infoHash`) for external players and browser-safe direct playback; `lib/streamPlan.ts` still routes browser-unsupported audio (→ AAC remux) and sub-4K HEVC (→ H.264 transcode) through ffmpeg for *completed* files, and 4K/UHD non-safe video to the external-player flow via the `movie://` scheme. Browser codec limits (H.264/VP9/AV1; no HEVC/.avi guarantee) still apply. `playinfo` also probes every audio/subtitle track for the browser-player upgrade. Packaging never re-encodes browser-safe AAC-LC audio (stream-copied) and runs renditions concurrently (S14); before packaging, Watch probes `mseProbe` codec strings and routes undecodable video (e.g. HEVC Main10) straight to the external-player screen. |
| D9 | Deployment: single `docker-compose.yml` with services `postgres`, `qbittorrent`, `prowlarr`, `backend`, `frontend`. Frontend served by nginx that proxies `/api` and `/socket.io` to the backend. |
| D10 | Cost: everything is free/open-source. Only required external account is a free TMDB API key; an **optional free OMDb key** (`OMDB_API_KEY`) enables portrait posters for the wide tiles (§4.6) — cards degrade to monograms when absent. |
| D11 | Testing: **Vitest** on the backend (unit tests with mocked providers); frontend smoke test via manual run in M4. |
| D12 | Magnet links: prefer Prowlarr-provided magnet; otherwise build from `infoHash` + 9 public trackers (list in `02-specs.md` §4.3). |
| D13 | LAN exposure: `frontend`, `qbittorrent` (Web UI), and `prowlarr` are all published on host ports (`0.0.0.0`). qBittorrent must have strong credentials (it has its own login); Prowlarr has no auth — documented risk accepted for a home LAN. `postgres` and `backend` stay internal-only. |
| D14 | TV browsing (v2): TV titles present TMDB **seasons/episodes**; contextual Prowlarr searches are whole-show (S3 no params), per-season (`?season=N` → season packs + episode releases), or per-episode (`?season=N&episode=M`). The Advanced picker retains the 30-row "Load more" + client-side filters/grouping from v1. **Friendly downloads auto-pick the most-seeded matching source**; releases with unparseable coverage are Advanced-only; a per-episode download never silently pulls a whole season. |
| D15 | Frontend visual language: **Netflix-style; black & white UI chrome over full-color artwork**. Left sidebar removed; fixed top header transparent at top that fades to a black gradient on scroll. Home = static cinematic brand hero + **16:9 full-bleed title-card tiles** (whole-card click, no captions/info icons) that bleed full-width with the rightmost card clipped to invite scroll; full-screen search overlay. Trailer metadata comes from TMDB `GET /movie/{id}/videos` / `GET /tv/{id}/videos` through the existing key — **no new key, no YouTube Data API, no backend storage** (`S15`). TV cards use the **series** trailer (per-episode trailers are not surfaced — TMDB coverage is sparse). The on-card presentation is **D20** (this entry no longer defines rendering). Embedding requires the *browser* to reach YouTube/Vimeo; the LAN box only needs TMDB reachability. |

Best-source search runs only when the title owns no copy, is deduped + cached in the API client per context (~10 min), and lazily re-fetches after the last copy is deleted. Releases of one movie are **versions of a single library item** (`lib/versions.ts` pure helpers + `store/versionStore` persisted to `localStorage` keyed `movie:<tmdbId>`; default rule = most recently completed playable copy, tie-break higher resolution): My Downloads shows one card per movie with hover version chips; the Downloads page groups copies under `Movie · N versions` headers and labels each row `audio · quality`. Downloads persist `audioLang`/`audioMode` (idempotent `ALTER`, `S4`) so copies differing only by language stay distinguishable. TV keeps its episode layout and only reuses the panel for the active season pack; the C-DL1 confirm sheet is unchanged. |
| D20 | **Expanded Netflix-style hover card (replaces D18's inline overlay)**: every `TitleCard` expands into a **portaled, fixed pop-up card** after a sustained ~600 ms hover — width **1.7×** the base card (viewport-clamped), **vertically centered on the base cell (grows equally above and below)** and horizontally centered so it **overflows the neighbouring cards on all four sides**, `z-index: 150`, 8 px radius + strong dark shadow; base card keeps its grid slot (no white ring/scale while open); any scroll/resize dismisses it. Split layout: **media top (16:9)** = autoplay-looped trailer with **sound ON by default** (Chrome silences unmuted autoplay until the user has clicked the app once) + circular mute/unmute button that **remounts the iframe** (clip restarts), title/logo bottom-left over a scrim; **details bottom (dark column)** = compact Netflix-matching panel (16 px gutters, ~1.35 line-height, medium-500 13 px text): row 1 = Play (white circle → primary Watch action when present, else Detail) + two **decorative no-op circles** (Add to List `+`, Rate thumbs-up) + More Info chevron; My-Downloads version chips sit on their **own row beneath the actions**; row 2 = monochrome age-badge (`certification`) · duration ("2h 15m") or season count ("N Seasons") · `HD` chip (all 1 px translucent outlines, ~11 px); row 3 = up to three genre tags joined by `•`. Typeface is self-hosted **Inter Variable** (proprietary **Netflix Sans** is never bundled) standing in for the Netflix look. Data arrives from **S16** (`GET /api/media/:id/hover`), one call returning trailer + genres + runtime + seasons + certification, cached client-side ~1 h; US rating comes from TMDB `release_dates`/`content_ratings`. ## Build order (how 03-tasks.md is sequenced)

Every milestone must be independently runnable and verifiable before the next starts:

1. Project scaffold (repo layout, tooling, config, docker-compose, CI if any).
2. Core domain logic that has no external dependencies (unit-testable first).
3. External integrations one at a time, each behind an interface (TMDB, Prowlarr, qBittorrent).
4. API layer over the domain logic (REST + Socket.IO).
5. UI layer.
6. End-to-end wiring, polish, and verification.

## Execution protocol

1. Agent reads `AGENTS.md`, then this file, then `03-tasks.md`.
2. Agent works through tasks **in order**. Each task names exactly which of the other docs to read.
3. After each task, the agent reports what it did and how the acceptance criteria were verified.
4. A human confirms each milestone before the next begins.

1: import type { MediaInfo } from './mediaInfo.js';
2: import type { MediaProbe } from './probe.js';
3: 
4: export type StreamMode = 'direct' | 'remux-audio' | 'transcode' | 'player-required';
5: /** Playback mode reported by playinfo. 'hls' = Shaka plays an HLS web package. */
6: export type PlaybackMode = StreamMode | 'hls';
7: 
8: const SAFE_VIDEO_CODECS = new Set(['h264', 'vp9', 'av1']);
9: const SAFE_AUDIO_CODECS = new Set(['aac', 'mp3', 'opus', 'flac']);
10: 
11: const UHD_HEIGHT = 2160;
12: 
13: /** Video codecs ffmpeg can stream-copy into an fMP4 HLS package. */
14: export const HLS_COPYABLE_VIDEO = new Set(['h264', 'hevc', 'vp9', 'av1']);
15: 
16: /** Containers the browser <video> element can demux natively (direct playback). */
17: const NATIVE_CONTAINERS = new Set(['mp4', 'webm', 'mov']);
18: 
19: /** Legacy decision used by the /watch raw-remux path (kept for compatibility). */
20: export function decideStreamMode(probe: MediaProbe): StreamMode {
21:   const video = probe.videoCodec?.toLowerCase() ?? null;
22:   const audio = probe.audioCodec?.toLowerCase() ?? null;
23:   const height = probe.height ?? 0;
24: 
25:   const videoSafe = video === null || SAFE_VIDEO_CODECS.has(video);
26:   const audioSafe = audio === null || SAFE_AUDIO_CODECS.has(audio);
27: 
28:   if (videoSafe && audioSafe) return 'direct';
29:   if (videoSafe) return 'remux-audio';
30:   if (height >= UHD_HEIGHT) return 'player-required';
31:   return 'transcode';
32: }
33: 
34: /**
35:  * Modern decision over the full media probe. `direct` only when the container
36:  * plays natively AND video + all audio tracks are browser-safe with nothing the
37:  * player would need extra tracks/subs for. Everything with a copyable video
38:  * codec gets packaged to HLS (container change, AAC audio per language, WebVTT
39:  * subtitles). Video codecs that cannot be stream-copied keep the legacy
40:  * transcode/external behavior.
41:  */
42: export function decidePlaybackMode(media: MediaInfo | null, extra?: { sidecarSubtitles?: number }): PlaybackMode {
43:   if (!media) return 'direct';
44:   const videoCodec = media.videoCodec?.toLowerCase() ?? null;
45:   const container = media.container?.toLowerCase() ?? null;
46:   const audioAllSafe =
47:     media.audioTracks.length === 0 || media.audioTracks.every((a) => SAFE_AUDIO_CODECS.has(a.codec?.toLowerCase() ?? ''));
48:   const singleAudio = media.audioTracks.length <= 1;
49:   const wantsExtraTracks =
50:     media.subtitleTracks.length > 0 || media.audioTracks.length > 1 || (extra?.sidecarSubtitles ?? 0) > 0;
51: 
52:   if (container && NATIVE_CONTAINERS.has(container) && videoCodec && SAFE_VIDEO_CODECS.has(videoCodec)) {
53:     if (audioAllSafe && singleAudio && !wantsExtraTracks) return 'direct';
54:   }
55: 
56:   if (videoCodec && HLS_COPYABLE_VIDEO.has(videoCodec)) {
57:     // 4K/UHD HEVC is stream-copied into an HLS package most browsers still can't
58:     // decode — keep the bit-perfect external-player flow for that case.
59:     if (videoCodec === 'hevc' && (media.height ?? 0) >= UHD_HEIGHT) return 'player-required';
60:     return 'hls';
61:   }
62: 
63:   const height = media.height ?? 0;
64:   if (height >= UHD_HEIGHT) return 'player-required';
65:   return 'transcode';
66: }

2: import type { AudioInfo, MediaInfo, SidecarSubtitle, SubtitleInfo } from './mediaInfo.js';

4: /**
5:  * Pure builders for the "web package" pipeline: converting a fully-downloaded
6:  * file into an HLS VOD package (video stream-copied, audio re-encoded to AAC per
7:  * track, text subtitles to WebVTT) that a MSE player (Shaka) can play with
8:  * audio-language and subtitle switching. No ffmpeg is invoked here — these
9:  * functions only describe the file layout, ffmpeg arguments and playlists so
10:  * they can be unit-tested.
11:  */
12: 
13: /** Deterministic directory key for one package (per torrent + file). */
14: export function packageKey(infoHash: string, relative: string): string {
15:   const slug = relative.split('/').join('-').replace(/[^A-Za-z0-9._-]/g, '-');
16:   return `${infoHash.toLowerCase()}-${slug}`;
17: }
18: 
19: const LANGUAGE_LABELS: Record<string, string> = {
20:   en: 'English',
21:   es: 'Español',
22:   pt: 'Português',
23:   fr: 'Français',
24:   de: 'Deutsch',
25:   it: 'Italiano',
26:   ja: '日本語',
27:   ko: '한국어',
28:   zh: '中文',
29:   ru: 'Русский',
30:   ar: 'العربية',
31:   hi: 'हिन्दी',
32:   nl: 'Nederlands',
33:   sv: 'Svenska',
34:   pl: 'Polski',
35:   tr: 'Türkçe',
36: };
37: 
38: export function languageLabel(language: string | null): string {
39:   if (language && LANGUAGE_LABELS[language]) return LANGUAGE_LABELS[language]!;
40:   return language ? language.toUpperCase() : 'Unknown';
41: }
42: 
43: /** Valid EXT-X-MEDIA LANGUAGE value; falls back to "und". */
44: export function hlsLanguage(language: string | null): string {
45:   return language && /^[a-z]{2,3}(-[A-Za-z0-9]+)*$/.test(language) ? language : 'und';
46: }
47: 
48: export interface AudioRendition {
49:   streamIndex: number;
50:   language: string | null;
51:   title: string | null;
52:   label: string;
53:   default: boolean;
54: }
55: 
56: export interface SubtitleRendition {
57:   id: string;
58:   language: string | null;
59:   label: string;
60: }
61: 
62: export function pickAudioRenditions(media: MediaInfo): AudioRendition[] {
63:   const firstDefault = media.audioTracks.find((a) => a.default) ?? media.audioTracks[0];
64:   return media.audioTracks.map((a: AudioInfo) => ({
65:     streamIndex: a.index,
66:     language: a.language,
67:     title: a.title,
68:     label: a.title || languageLabel(a.language),
69:     default: a === firstDefault || media.audioTracks.length === 1,
70:   }));
71: }
72: 
73: export function pickSubtitleRenditions(
74:   tracks: SubtitleInfo[],
75:   sidecars: SidecarSubtitle[],
76: ): SubtitleRendition[] {
77:   const textTracks = tracks
78:     .filter((s) => s.kind === 'text')
79:     .map((s, i) => ({
80:       id: `track-${i}`,
81:       language: s.language,
82:       label: s.title || languageLabel(s.language),
83:     }));
84:   const sidecar = sidecars.map((s, i) => ({
85:     id: `sidecar-${i}`,
86:     language: s.language,
87:     label: languageLabel(s.language) || s.name.replace(/\.(srt|ass|ssa|vtt)$/i, ''),
88:   }));
89:   return [...textTracks, ...sidecar];
90: }
91: 
92: /** fMP4 HLS segments, ~6s each, VOD (static) playlist written to `<dir>/main.m3u8`. */
93: export function videoSegmentArgs(input: string, dir: string): string[] {
94:   return [
95:     '-hide_banner',
96:     '-loglevel', 'error',
97:     '-i', input,
98:     '-map', '0:v:0',
99:     '-c:v', 'copy',
100:     '-an', '-dn',
101:     '-f', 'hls',
102:     '-hls_time', '6',
103:     '-hls_playlist_type', 'vod',
104:     '-hls_segment_type', 'fmp4',
105:     '-hls_fmp4_init_filename', 'init.mp4',
106:     '-hls_segment_filename', path.join(dir, 'seg_%05d.m4s'),
107:     path.join(dir, 'main.m3u8'),
108:   ];
109: }
110: 
111: /**
112:  * A browser-safe AAC track can be stream-copied into the fMP4 rendition —
113:  * re-encoding it (AAC → AAC) wastes minutes of single-core CPU for no gain.
114:  * Only AAC-LC ≤ 48 kHz is copied; HE-AAC (SBR/PS) keeps its container codec
115:  * quirks that MSE players don't handle, so it is still re-encoded.
116:  */
117: export function canCopyAudioTrack(track: { codec?: string | null; profile?: string | null; sampleRate?: number | null }): boolean {
118:   if ((track.codec ?? '').toLowerCase() !== 'aac') return false;
119:   const profile = (track.profile ?? '').toLowerCase();
120:   if (profile && profile !== 'lc') return false;
121:   const rate = track.sampleRate;
122:   return rate == null || (rate > 0 && rate <= 48000);
123: }
124: 
125: /** One audio track → AAC, separate fMP4 HLS rendition in `<dir>/main.m3u8`. */
126: export function audioSegmentArgs(
127:   input: string,
128:   streamIndex: number,
129:   dir: string,
130:   opts: { copy?: boolean } = {},
131: ): string[] {
132:   const encode = opts.copy
133:     ? ['-c:a', 'copy']
134:     : ['-c:a', 'aac', '-b:a', '192k', '-aac_coder', 'fast'];
135:   return [
136:     '-hide_banner',
137:     '-loglevel', 'error',
138:     '-i', input,
139:     '-map', `0:${streamIndex}`,
140:     ...encode,
141:     '-f', 'hls',
142:     '-hls_time', '6',
143:     '-hls_playlist_type', 'vod',
144:     '-hls_segment_type', 'fmp4',
145:     '-hls_fmp4_init_filename', 'init.mp4',
146:     '-hls_segment_filename', path.join(dir, 'seg_%05d.m4s'),
147:     path.join(dir, 'main.m3u8'),
148:   ];
149: }
150: 
151: /** Convert an embedded text subtitle stream to a single WebVTT file. */
152: export function embeddedSubtitleArgs(input: string, streamIndex: number, out: string): string[] {
153:   return [
154:     '-hide_banner',
155:     '-loglevel', 'error',
156:     '-y',
157:     '-i', input,
158:     '-map', `0:${streamIndex}`,
159:     '-c:s', 'webvtt',
160:     '-f', 'webvtt',
161:     out,
162:   ];
163: }
164: 
165: /** Convert a sidecar subtitle file (srt/ass/…) to a single WebVTT file. */
166: export function sidecarSubtitleArgs(sidecar: string, out: string): string[] {
167:   return [
168:     '-hide_banner',
169:     '-loglevel', 'error',
170:     '-y',
171:     '-i', sidecar,
172:     '-map', '0:0',
173:     '-c:s', 'webvtt',
174:     '-f', 'webvtt',
175:     out,
176:   ];
177: }
178: 
179: /**
180:  * HLS subtitle media playlist that references a single whole-file WebVTT
181:  * segment. Kept deliberately simple: one #EXTINF covering the media duration.
182:  */
183: export function subtitleMediaPlaylist(durationSeconds: number | null, fileName = 'subs.vtt'): string {
184:   const duration = durationSeconds && durationSeconds > 0 ? durationSeconds : 600;
185:   const target = Math.ceil(duration);
186:   const inf = duration.toFixed(3);
187:   return [
188:     '#EXTM3U',
189:     '#EXT-X-VERSION:6',
190:     '#EXT-X-PLAYLIST-TYPE:VOD',
191:     '#EXT-X-MEDIA-SEQUENCE:0',
192:     `#EXT-X-TARGETDURATION:${target}`,
193:     `#EXTINF:${inf},`,
194:     fileName,
195:     '#EXT-X-ENDLIST',
196:     '',
197:   ].join('\n');
198: }
199: 
200: export interface MasterOptions {
201:   durationSeconds: number | null;
202:   audio: AudioRendition[];
203:   subtitles: SubtitleRendition[];
204:   /** Estimated bandwidth of the video rendition (video-only), e.g. from bytes/duration. */
205:   bandwidth: number | null;
206:   /** video stream's codec name (h264/hevc/…) for the CODECS hint (optional). */
207:   videoCodec?: string | null;
208:   resolution?: { width: number | null; height: number | null } | null;
209: }
210: 
211: /**
212:  * Author the master playlist. The main rendition is VIDEO-ONLY (all audio lives
213:  * in the AUDIO group so Shaka can switch languages); subtitles come from a
214:  * SUBTITLES group pointing at per-track subtitle media playlists.
215:  */
216: export function buildMasterPlaylist(opts: MasterOptions): string {
217:   const lines: string[] = ['#EXTM3U', '#EXT-X-VERSION:6', '#EXT-X-INDEPENDENT-SEGMENTS'];
218:   const hasAudio = opts.audio.length > 0;
219:   const hasSubs = opts.subtitles.length > 0;
220: 
221:   if (hasAudio) {
222:     opts.audio.forEach((audio) => {
223:       const attrs = [
224:         `TYPE=AUDIO`,
225:         `GROUP-ID="aud"`,
226:         `NAME="${quoteAttr(audio.label)}"`,
227:         `LANGUAGE="${hlsLanguage(audio.language)}"`,
228:         audio.default ? 'DEFAULT=YES' : 'DEFAULT=NO',
229:         'AUTOSELECT=YES',
230:         `URI="audio/${audio.streamIndex}/main.m3u8"`,
231:       ];
232:       lines.push(`#EXT-X-MEDIA:${attrs.join(',')}`);
233:     });
234:   }
235: 
236:   if (hasSubs) {
237:     opts.subtitles.forEach((sub) => {
238:       const attrs = [
239:         `TYPE=SUBTITLES`,
240:         `GROUP-ID="subs"`,
241:         `NAME="${quoteAttr(sub.label)}"`,
242:         `LANGUAGE="${hlsLanguage(sub.language)}"`,
243:         'DEFAULT=NO',
244:         'AUTOSELECT=YES',
245:         `URI="subs/${sub.id}.m3u8"`,
246:       ];
247:       lines.push(`#EXT-X-MEDIA:${attrs.join(',')}`);
248:     });
249:   }
250: 
251:   const streamAttrs = ['BANDWIDTH=4000000'];
252:   if (opts.videoCodec) streamAttrs.push(`CODECS="${codecsHint(opts.videoCodec, hasAudio)}"`);
253:   if (opts.resolution?.width && opts.resolution.height) {
254:     streamAttrs.push(`RESOLUTION=${opts.resolution.width}x${opts.resolution.height}`);
255:   }
256:   if (hasAudio) streamAttrs.push('AUDIO="aud"');
257:   if (hasSubs) streamAttrs.push('SUBTITLES="subs"');
258:   lines.push(`#EXT-X-STREAM-INF:${streamAttrs.join(',')}`);
259:   lines.push('video/main.m3u8');
260:   lines.push('');
261:   return lines.join('\n');
262: }
263: 
264: function quoteAttr(value: string): string {
265:   return value.replace(/"/g, '');
266: }
267: 
268: /** Keep CODECS minimal: the AAC encoder emits mp4a.40.2; video codec is best-effort. */
269: function codecsHint(videoCodec: string, hasAudio: boolean): string {
270:   const video = videoCodecNameToCodecs(videoCodec);
271:   return hasAudio ? `${video},mp4a.40.2` : video;
272: }
273: 
274: function videoCodecNameToCodecs(codec: string): string {
275:   switch (codec.toLowerCase()) {
276:     case 'h264':
277:       return 'avc1.640028';
278:     case 'hevc':
279:       return 'hvc1.1.6.L93.B0';
280:     case 'vp9':
281:       return 'vp09.00.10.08';
282:     case 'av1':
283:       return 'av01.0.04M.08';
284:     default:
285:       return codec;
286:   }
287: }
288: 
289: /**
290:  * MediaSource type strings (one per codec-string spelling) that describe a
291:  * packaged HLS rendition's video track (+ its always-AAC audio). The browser
292:  * preflight probes these with `MediaSource.isTypeSupported` *before* any
293:  * packaging starts, so content the browser can never decode (e.g. HEVC
294:  * Main10 in Chrome/Firefox) is routed straight to the external-player flow
295:  * instead of paying for a doomed package build.
296:  *
297:  * Returns `[]` when the codec is definitely not browser-decodable, so callers
298:  * can short-circuit to the player screen.
299:  */
300: export interface MseVideoProbe {
301:   codec: string | null;
302:   profile?: string | null;
303:   level?: number | null;
304:   pixFmt?: string | null;
305: }
306: 
307: export function mseProbeTypes(video: MseVideoProbe | null): string[] {
308:   if (!video || !video.codec) return [];
309:   const codec = video.codec.toLowerCase();
310:   const audio = ',mp4a.40.2';
311:   switch (codec) {
312:     case 'h264':
313:     case 'avc1':
314:       return [`video/mp4; codecs="avc1.640028${audio}"`, `video/mp4; codecs="avc1.4d401f${audio}"`];
315:     case 'vp9':
316:       return [`video/mp4; codecs="vp09.00.10.08${audio}"`];
317:     case 'av1':
318:       return [`video/mp4; codecs="av01.0.04M.08${audio}"`];
319:     case 'hevc':
320:     case 'h265': {
321:       if (hevcBeyondBrowserSupport(video)) return [];
322:       const level = hevcLevelIdc(video.level);
323:       return [
324:         `video/mp4; codecs="hvc1.1.6.L${level}.B0${audio}"`,
325:         `video/mp4; codecs="hev1.1.6.L${level}.B0${audio}"`,
326:       ];
327:     }
328:     default:
329:       // Unknown/legacy codecs never reach hls packaging (they go to
330:       // transcode/player-required instead) — stay permissive.
331:       return [];
332:   }
333: }
334: 
335: /** Chrome/Firefox cannot decode HEVC beyond 8-bit Main; detect and gate out. */
336: function hevcBeyondBrowserSupport(video: MseVideoProbe): boolean {
337:   const pix = (video.pixFmt ?? '').toLowerCase();
338:   const profile = (video.profile ?? '').toLowerCase();
339:   if (/(p0?10|p0?12|10le|12le|yuv420p10|yuv444)/.test(pix)) return true;
340:   if (/main\s*10|main10|12|rext|422|444/.test(profile)) return true;
341:   return false;
342: }
343: 
344: /** ffprobe HEVC `level` is level * 30 (e.g. 120 = 4.0); default to a safe 3.1. */
345: function hevcLevelIdc(level: number | null | undefined): number {
346:   return typeof level === 'number' && level > 0 ? level : 93;
347: }

350:   key: string;
351:   root: string;
352:   videoDir: string;
353:   audioDir: (streamIndex: number) => string;
354:   subsDir: string;
355: }

358:   const root = path.join(packageRoot, key);
359:   return {
360:     key,
361:     root,
362:     videoDir: path.join(root, 'video'),
363:     audioDir: (streamIndex: number) => path.join(root, 'audio', String(streamIndex)),
364:     subsDir: path.join(root, 'subs'),
365:   };
366: }

display.text:
name: movie-downloader

services:
  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: app
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: app
      POSTGRES_DB: moviedl
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U app -d moviedl"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 12
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [internal]

  qbittorrent:
    image: linuxserver/qbittorrent
    environment:
      PUID: "1000"
      PGID: "1000"
      TZ: Etc/UTC
      WEBUI_PORT: "8080"
    volumes:
      - qbconfig:/config
      - downloads:/downloads
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
      - "6881:6881"
      - "6881:6881/udp"
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [internal]

  prowlarr:
    image: linuxserver/prowlarr
    environment:
      PUID: "1000"
      PGID: "1000"
      TZ: Etc/UTC
      # Used by deploy/prowlarr-api-key.sh (mounted below) to pin the API key in
      # config.xml on every boot, so it can never drift from the backend's
      # PROWLARR_API_KEY when the prowlarr-config volume is recreated.
      PROWLARR_API_KEY: ${PROWLARR_API_KEY:?set PROWLARR_API_KEY in .env}
    volumes:
      - prowlarr-config:/config
      # linuxserver/prowlarr ignores PROWLARR__* env overrides; this init script
      # seeds/patches config.xml before Prowlarr starts.
      - ./deploy/prowlarr-api-key.sh:/custom-cont-init.d/99-prowlarr-api-key.sh:ro
    ports:
      - "9696:9696"
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [internal]

  flaresolverr:
    image: ghcr.io/flaresolverr/flaresolverr:latest
    environment:
      LOG_LEVEL: info
      TZ: Etc/UTC
    ports:
      - "8191:8191"
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [internal]

  backend:
    build: ./backend
    extra_hosts:
      # Some ISP/host DNS servers return a dead BunnyCDN edge for image.tmdb.org
      # (TCP times out). Pin a reachable edge; any BunnyCDN node serves the same images.
      - "image.tmdb.org:152.233.22.97"
    environment:
      TMDB_API_KEY: ${TMDB_API_KEY:?set TMDB_API_KEY in .env}
      OMDB_API_KEY: ${OMDB_API_KEY:-}
      PROWLARR_URL: http://prowlarr:9696
      PROWLARR_API_KEY: ${PROWLARR_API_KEY:?set PROWLARR_API_KEY in .env}
      QBITTORRENT_URL: http://qbittorrent:8080
      QBITTORRENT_USER: ${QBITTORRENT_USER:-admin}
      QBITTORRENT_PASS: ${QBITTORRENT_PASS:?set QBITTORRENT_PASS in .env}
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://app:app@postgres:5432/moviedl
      DOWNLOAD_DIR: /downloads
      PORT: "3000"
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
    volumes:
      - downloads:/downloads
      - packages:/packages
      - art:/art
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [internal]

  frontend:
    build: ./frontend
    ports:
      - "5173:80"
    depends_on:
      - backend
    restart: unless-stopped
    networks: [internal]

volumes:
  pgdata:
  qbconfig:
  prowlarr-config:
  downloads:
  packages:
  art:

networks:
  internal:
    driver: bridge

- Behavior: looks up the matching `art_files` row, resolves `file_path` inside `ART_DIR` (path comes from the DB — never from the request; containment-checked), and streams the file with `Content-Type` from its extension and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
- Response: `200` image bytes; `404` unknown subject or file missing from disk.
- Warm-on-miss: when no usable row exists the route asks the poster pipeline (§4.8) to warm the subject once (synchronously) before responding — so a card's first render resolves its own poster without waiting for the warm loop. Titles with no poster are recorded `empty` and answered `404` fast until the retry window elapses.
- Fallback contract: the frontend treats this route as the **only** card/hero art source; a `404`/`onError` shows the monogram placeholder (it never falls back to TMDB/FanArt imagery).

### S9 Socket.IO events
- Namespace: default (`/`).
- On connect, server emits `downloads:initial` with `{ downloads: DownloadRecord[] }`.
- Every 2s, server emits `downloads:update` with `{ downloads: DownloadRecord[] }`.
- Client never sends messages (subscribe-only).
- During each poll cycle the server: syncs `torrent_name`/`size_bytes` from qBittorrent, **adopts the real qBittorrent `hash` for any `downloads` row keyed by a `url-` placeholder by matching `torrent_name`** (torrents added via a Prowlarr download URL have no infohash up-front), resolves `stream_file_path`/`streamable` only when a **fully-downloaded (non-`.!qb`) video file** exists under `content_path` (never for partials), sets `completed_at` on `progress == 1` transition, and maps `eta == -1` to null before emitting.

### S10 `GET /api/downloads/:infoHash/file`
- Auth: none
- Behavior: resolves the same fully-downloaded media file as `S7` but streams it as an attachment (`Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="<basename>"`). Used as the fallback for external playback when the browser can't decode a codec or no `movie://` handler is registered. Path containment per NFR9.
- Response: `200` file download (no Range guarantee needed).
- Errors: `404` unknown `infoHash` / no complete resolvable file.

### S11 `POST /api/downloads/:infoHash/pause` · `POST /api/downloads/:infoHash/resume`
- Auth: none
- Behavior: pauses/resumes the torrent in qBittorrent (`/api/v2/torrents/stop|start`). State updates arrive on the next Socket.IO snapshot.
- Response: `204`.
- Errors: `404` unknown `infoHash`; `502` qBittorrent unreachable/failed.

### S12 `GET /api/media/:id/season/:seasonNumber`
- Auth: none
- Request: params `id`, `seasonNumber`; query `type=tv` (required).
- Behavior: fetches `/tv/{id}/season/{n}` from TMDB and maps each episode to `TvEpisode`.
- Response: `200` → `{ season: TvSeasonSummary, episodes: TvEpisode[] }` where `TvEpisode = { seasonNumber: number, episodeNumber: number, name: string, overview: string, stillPath: string|null, runtime: number|null, airDate: string|null }`. Empty season → `episodes: []`.
- Errors: `400` missing/invalid `type` or `seasonNumber`; `404` season not found; `502` TMDB unreachable.

### S13 `GET /api/downloads/:infoHash/files`
- Auth: none
- Behavior: resolves the torrent's `content_path` and lists its playable video files (same resolver as §4.4). Each file's basename is parsed server-side with the §4.5 regex so the UI never re-implements episode parsing.
- Response: `200` → `{ files: StreamFileInfo[] }` where `StreamFileInfo = { relative: string, mime: string, size: number, complete: boolean, seasonNumber: number|null, episodeNumber: number|null }`.
- Errors: `404` unknown `infoHash` or `content_path` not ready.

### S14 HLS web package (browser-player upgrade, Shaka)
- Auth: none. Only complete files resolve.
- `GET /api/playback/:infoHash/hls/status` (`?file=` optional): resolves the file, ensures a package run is started (idempotent, one ffmpeg job per file), returns `{ phase: "packaging"|"ready"|"failed", progress: 0–1, error: string|null }`.
- `GET /api/playback/:infoHash/hls/master.m3u8`: when ready → the authored master playlist (`application/vnd.apple.mpegurl`); while packaging → `202` + status body; failed → the failed status.
- `DELETE /api/playback/:infoHash/hls`: deletes the cached package (used for a failed-package retry).
- `GET /api/playback/pkg/:key/*`: serves the package's segments/init/subtitle files. `key` must match a package key (hash + slug); paths are containment-checked.
- Packaging (`lib/hls.ts` + `lib/packages.ts`, cache root `PACKAGE_DIR` default `/packages` on a `packages` compose volume): ffmpeg **stream-copies video and any browser-safe AAC-LC ≤48 kHz audio track** (`-c:a copy`), re-encodes only non-safe audio to AAC (`aac 192k` with the fast coder) into separate HLS audio renditions, converts embedded text + sidecar subtitles to WebVTT, then writes `video/main.m3u8`, `audio/<idx>/main.m3u8`, `subs/<id>.{vtt,m3u8}` and a `master.m3u8` with EXT-X-MEDIA AUDIO/SUBTITLES groups. Media renditions run as **concurrent ffmpeg processes** (one full-file pass each, parallel across cores) rather than serialized passes; in-flight progress is read from each process's `-progress` output so the bar moves during long encodes. Done marker makes cached packages reusable across restarts. Packages are removed on torrent delete (S6).
- **MSE preflight (S7b `mseProbe`)**: before any packaging starts, the browser probes `MediaSource.isTypeSupported` against the returned codec strings. Unsupported video (e.g. HEVC **Main10 / 10-bit**, which Chrome/Firefox cannot decode) → Watch renders the player-required screen instantly with the codec reason and **never starts a package build** the browser could not play.
- Watch plays `mode:"hls"` through **Shaka Player** (lazy-loaded `shaka-player`, its own controls overlay with audio-language/subtitle menus) after polling `status`; packaging/failure states show progress or external-player/Download-file fallbacks.

### S15 `GET /api/media/:id/trailer`
- Auth: none.
- Request: query `type: "movie" | "tv"` (required).

# T-006 — Web-streaming decision (spike output)

Date: 2026-09-07. Status: **approved by spike (T-006)**. Implementation lives in the
follow-up ticket T-007. This document records the spike's verification and costing,
compares the candidate strategies, and states the decision. No production code was
changed by the spike itself.

## 1. Problem restated

Some fully-downloaded movies cannot be watched in the in-browser player. Real cases in
this install: **The Dark Knight ("Batman")** and **Blade Runner 2049** are unplayable;
**X-Men '97** plays fine. The author remembered that "before [the Shaka player],
ffmpeg-based playback seemed to play more video types", and asked whether Shaka is the
right choice and whether it is well configured.

The spike verified the root-cause hypothesis on the real files, measured the CPU/disk
cost of the candidate strategies on this host, and picked one.

## 2. Real-file verification (acceptance criterion 1)

All three problem files were probed with the app's own pipeline: `ffprobe` full
stream dump (identical args to `lib/mediaInfo.ts`) plus the live `playinfo` response
(`S7b`) from the running backend, and the frontend gating decision was traced in code.

| File (download row) | ffprobe video | audio / subs | `playinfo` mode | `mseProbe` | In-browser result |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| The Dark Knight (tmdb 155, row 9) `1080p.BluRay.x265.10bit-GalaxyRG265.mkv` | **hevc · Main 10 · yuv420p10le · level 120 · 1920×1080** · bt709, 2h32m, 4.0 GB | eac3 5.1; 1 subrip | `hls` | `[]` | **player screen** (`hls && !canPlayHls`) |
| Blade Runner 2049 (tmdb 335984, row 8) `1080p...x265.10bit-KONTRAST.mp4` | **hevc · Main 10 · yuv420p10le · level 120 · 1920×1080** · bt709, 2h44m, 4.8 GB | aac-lc 5.1; none | `hls` | `[]` | **player screen** |
| X-Men '97 S01E01 (tmdb 138502, row 10) | h264 · High · yuv420p · 1280×720 · level 31 | aac-lc 2ch; 24 text subs | `hls` | `[avc1.640028…, avc1.4d401f…]` | **plays** (fast copy package) |

Extra real data points found on the same volume (no DB rows): The Dark Knight 4K REMUX
`2160p...HDR10 DV...REMUX` = hevc · Main 10 · yuv420p10le · **3840×2160** · smpte2084
(59 GB) — the 4K-class file; The Odyssey 1080p TELESYNC = hevc · Main 10 ·
yuv420p10le · 1920×1000 — another ≤1080p 10-bit file; Oppenheimer 4K = hevc 2160p HDR.

### Verdict on the hypothesis: **confirmed**

1. Every unplayable file is **HEVC (x265) 10-bit at ≤1080p** (Main 10 /
   yuv420p10le). For these, `lib/hls.ts` `hevcBeyondBrowserSupport()` returns true, so
   `mseProbeTypes()` yields `[]` and the live `playinfo` answers `mseProbe: []`.
2. `WatchPage.tsx:31-39` (`canPlayHlsInBrowser`) → `codecUnsupported` → the
   `hls && codecUnsupported` branch at `WatchPage.tsx:219-220` renders the "Open in
   your player" screen (`:340`). The ffmpeg transcode fallback that existed pre-Shaka
   is **never offered** for these files.
3. Pre-Shaka behavior (`docs/plan/00-index.md` D8 / `lib/streamPlan.ts`
   `decideStreamMode`) had a catch-all `transcode` branch for **sub-2160p** non-safe
   video (`:30-31`), live re-encoding HEVC ≤1080p to H.264 via `/api/stream/:hash/watch`
   (`stream.ts:99-125`, `lib/transcode.ts`). **4K/UHD HEVC was `player-required` in
   both eras** (`decideStreamMode :30`, and `decidePlaybackMode :59` for 4K), so 4K
   never played in-browser either way.
4. The author's memory is correct: the pre-Shaka path played 1080p/720p HEVC by live
   re-encode — at the cost of per-play CPU, no seeking, and one generic audio stream.

X-Men '97 confirms the good path: h264 video is packaged by stream-copy in seconds and
plays through Shaka with its full language/subtitle menus.

Additional note for the follow-up: on Linux Chrome/Firefox the MSE probe also fails for
**plain 8-bit HEVC** (no HEVC decode at all, `MediaSource.isTypeSupported` false), so
the compatibility path must be gated on the browser probe, not on bit depth alone. The
existing frontend probe (`mseProbe` strings) already implements exactly that check.

## 3. Host and benchmark setup

- Host: **AMD Ryzen 7 5700U** (8 cores / 16 threads), 14 GB RAM, normal single-user
  home box running the whole Docker stack plus desktop load. Backend container = the
  app's own image (Alpine ffmpeg 8.0.1, **software decode/encode only** — no GPU
  passthrough in `docker-compose.yml`). ffprobe/ffmpeg confirmed able to decode
  10-bit HEVC Main 10 (`yuv420p10le`) — required for any transcode strategy.
- The host was shared during the spike (other agents/tooling at load ~19-37), so each
  number is reported with the load at measurement; low-load runs are the fair ones.

### Measured cost of H.264 re-encode on the real files

Command: the app's exact encoder profile — `libx264 -preset veryfast -crf 21
-pix_fmt yuv420p`, audio `aac 192k` (`lib/transcode.ts`, `lib/hls.ts` audio args).

| Measure | Run | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1080p HEVC-Main10 → H.264, first 120 s (host busy, load ≈30) | The Dark Knight | 120 s content in **70.6 s wall ≈ 1.7× realtime** |
| Same, first 60 s (load ≈19) | The Dark Knight | 60 s in **21 s wall ≈ 2.9× realtime** |
| Same, full-file background fMP4 package build (load ≈24-27) | The Dark Knight | sustained ≈2.0× realtime (61 segs/177 s at check); full 2h32m ≈ **70-80 min wall** |
| 2160p HEVC-Main10 → scaled 1080p H.264, 45 s (load ≈24, one package build running) | Dark Knight 4K REMUX | 45 s in 49 s wall ≈ **0.9× realtime**; full 2h32m ≈ **>2.5 h wall** |
| 4K decode at ≤2 GB free RAM, uncapped threads | Dark Knight 4K REMUX | **OOM-killed** (frame-threaded 2160p decode balloons RAM); thread-capped/paced runs are fine |

Pure decode-only runs of 1080p 10-bit measured 0.4-0.6× realtime while the host was
swapping — an artifact of the frame-threaded decoder ballooning memory into a
fast sink, not a representative number; the encode pipeline (which paces the decoder)
is the authoritative figure above.

### Measured disk cost (CRF21 veryfast, 1080p)

- Pipe to fragmented mp4 (the `/watch` live command): ≈3.95 Mb/s total.
- Full-file fMP4 HLS package (strategy A layout): ≈4.3 Mb/s video (64 MB per 120 s →
  ~0.5 MB/s). For a 2h32m film: **≈4.5-4.7 GB** package vs **4.3 GB** source
  (x265 10-bit CRF≈source size). A compat package therefore roughly **+1.1× the
  source file's size** on the `packages` volume. Audio renditions add only ~220 MB/h
  (192 kb/s AAC); WebVTT subs are negligible.
- 2160p→1080p capped rendition output: ≈3.5 Mb/s → ≈4.0 GB per 2h32m 4K film.

## 4. Candidate strategies — costed comparison

Key: **CPU** is the scarce resource (8 real cores, software codecs). Seekability,
latency, and menu quality are the user-visible differentiators.

### A. Keep Shaka/HLS; add a background H.264 "compatibility package" with auto-fallback

For any completed file the browser cannot decode whose video is ≤1080p (real case:
HEVC Main10 1080p/720p), build a **cached HLS package whose video rendition is
H.264** (same layout/pipeline as today's S14 packages — video step swapped from
`-c:v copy` to the measured libx264 encode; audio/subtitles unchanged). The MSE
preflight that today short-circuits to the player screen instead offers/starts the
compat package automatically; a cancel/bit-perfect path stays.

- **CPU**: one burst of ~70-80 min wall on this host per 2h32m 1080p HEVC file
  (~1.7-2.9× realtime, whole box), then **zero per replay** (cached, `DONE` marker,
  deleted with the torrent today). One build at a time + never during a live `/watch`
  stream keeps the box usable; the 2 s qBittorrent poll is unaffected (negligible CPU).
- **Disk**: ~+4.5-4.7 GB per such film on the existing `packages` volume (≈1.1× source).
  Needs an eviction/size budget beyond today's delete-on-torrent-delete.
- **Seek**: full VOD seeking via Shaka — same as today's good packages. No seeking
  regression.
- **Latency**: first watch pays the build (visible progress bar, as today — but ~1 h,
  not ~8 s, so the UI must be honest and cancellable to the local player); later
  watches are near-instant.
- **Quality**: one lossy encode (H.264 CRF21 — visually near-transparent for typical
  1080p; 10-bit→8-bit banding is the theoretical edge). All original audio tracks and
  text subtitles are preserved with per-language menus (Shaka).
- **Compatibility width**: restores the pre-Shaka universality for ≤1080p (HEVC 8/10
  bit, and incidentally any other non-browser-decodable ≤1080p codec that today hits
  the legacy live `transcode` branch).

### B. Drop Shaka; route everything through live `/watch` ffmpeg (the old behavior)

- **CPU**: identical encoder, but **per play** — every watch of a 2h32m HEVC film
  burns ~50-90 min of box CPU at ~1.7-2.9× realtime headroom. Two concurrent watches
  (or a watch + a background task) risk falling below realtime → stalls.
- **Disk**: none.
- **Seek**: none for transcoded files (progressive pipe, restart-to-seek) — a
  regression versus today's *seekable* direct/HLS good path.
- **Latency**: lowest start for the currently-unplayable class (no build), but no seek
  and restart-from-zero.
- **Quality**: same single lossy encode as A, plus only the first audio track and no
  subtitle menus — loses Shaka's per-language/subtitle UI on every file it touches.
  To avoid regressing the good h264 path you must keep Shaka anyway, which reduces B
  to "A without the cache" — strictly worse CPU and UX for the same code.

### C. Keep as-is; make the player-required screen the experience (depends on T-001)

- **CPU/disk**: zero new cost. **Result**: the in-browser player stays unable to play
  the most common movie encodes on this install (HEVC-Main10 1080p — the default
  release tier for films), and in-browser playback keeps depending on T-001 for every
  such file. X-Men-class files keep working.

## 5. Decision

**Adopt A** — keep Shaka/HLS as the player, and add an **on-demand, cached H.264
"compatibility package"** that auto-falls-back for completed ≤1080p files the
browser's MSE cannot decode (HEVC Main/Main10 and other non-decodable ≤1080p video),
with the external-player "Open in your player" flow retained as a first-class cancel
path.

The optional **4K → capped-1080p web rendition is deferred (out of the core
implementation, recorded as a possible later extension)**: 4K never played in-browser
in any era (bit-perfect external playback is the existing answer); on this host it
costs >2.5 h of CPU and ~4 GB per film with realtime-only headroom and OOM risk on a
low-RAM box. Not worth it for a single-user LAN app while T-001 covers 4K.

Rationale tied to this repo's constraints:

1. **Single-user self-host**: a one-time background cost (A) is affordable; the
   per-play live cost of B is the same CPU spent over and over. On 8 real cores,
   B's realtime headroom is the thing that breaks first.
2. **PACKAGE_DIR volume + S14 pipeline already exist**: A reuses the package manager,
   caching, `DONE`-marker, concurrency-aware progress, and delete-on-torrent-delete
   with a video-step change and a codec/browser gate. No new storage architecture.
3. **ffmpeg in the app image already decodes 10-bit HEVC** (software) — verified; no
   image change, no GPU dependency.
4. **No regression to the good path**: h264/vp9/av1 direct/HLS, AAC stream-copy, and
   per-language/subtitle menus are untouched; only files today condemned to the
   player screen gain a new in-browser route. A also shrinks the urgency of T-001/T-003
   without removing them.
5. **Codec normalization out of scope**: browsers on Linux cannot gain HEVC decode, so
   the compat package encodes *to* what browsers decode rather than fixing HEVC.

### Consequence for the follow-up ticket (T-007)

- New route/flag that asks the package manager for a **compat variant** of a package
  (video rendition re-encoded to H.264 CRF21 veryfast) triggered when the browser's
  MSE cannot decode the file's own video and height < 2160.
- WatchPage: the `hls && codecUnsupported` branch becomes a **"building a web-compatible
  copy"** state (progress, cancel → local player), never a dead end.
- Guardrails: at most one compat build at a time, and it must not starve a live
  `/watch` stream or the 2 s qBittorrent poll (poll CPU is negligible either way).
- Disk: eviction/size policy for the `packages` volume (compat packages are ~1.1× the
  source's size).
- 4K (>2160p or 2160p non-decodable): unchanged, stays on the external-player flow.
- External-player + Download-file stay reachable from every Watch state.

## 6. What was NOT changed

No production code (backend or frontend) was modified by this spike. Benchmark artifacts
lived in the backend container's `/tmp` and were removed.

| D21 | **Netflix-style wide tiles from OMDb portraits — the winning card-art source.** Research: no free API serves *wide* per-title studio art except TMDB backdrops/FanArt (Netflix title cards are proprietary; OMDb returns only a portrait `Poster`). Decision: **wide 16:9 tile composited in-app from the OMDb portrait** — crisp portrait figure at full tile height over its own blurred ground; used everywhere (rails, My Downloads, downloads page, search, Detail hero as blurred ground). Pipeline: TMDB external_ids `imdbId` → OMDb (`OMDB_API_KEY`, budgeted ~850 req/day) → Amazon portrait downloaded once to the `art` volume (`art_files`, kind `poster`) → served by S8b, which **warms on first miss**; `empty` rows cached 7 days; no poster → monogram (never TMDB/FanArt imagery). **FanArt.tv and the whole artwork-settings cluster are deleted** (provider toggle, per-size preference, `cardStyle` A/B, preview tester, `ART_GRID` spike, `FANART_API_KEY`, `media_art`); `/api/settings` is audio-only; Settings shows no artwork controls. S8 TMDB proxy remains only for TV episode stills. |
| D22 | **Web streaming: keep Shaka/HLS + add a cached H.264 "compatibility package" with auto-fallback (T-006 spike decision; implementation in T-007).** Real-file verification confirmed the root cause: every unplayable download here is **HEVC Main 10/10-bit ≤1080p** (`mseProbe: []`), so the Watch preflight sends it to the player screen and the pre-Shaka transcode fallback is never offered. External-player ("Open in your player") stays reachable from every Watch state. **Capped 1080p rendition for 4K is deferred**: measured >2.5 h CPU + ~4 GB/film with OOM risk on low RAM, and 4K never played in-browser in any era (bit-perfect external playback is the answer). Guardrails for T-007: one compat build at a time, never starving a live `/watch` stream or the 2 s qBittorrent poll (negligible either way); a `packages`-volume eviction/size policy. The good path (h264/vp9/av1 direct/HLS, AAC stream-copy, per-language/subtitle menus) is unchanged. |

## Change log

| Date | Change |
|------|--------|
| 2026-09-07 (streaming spike) | **Web-streaming decision (T-006 spike → D22, implementation in T-007)**: verified on the real downloads why some files can't play in-browser — The Dark Knight and Blade Runner 2049 are HEVC **Main 10 / yuv420p10le** at 1080p, whose `mseProbe` is `[]`, so the Watch MSE preflight (added in the 2026-09-06 playback-speed pass) routes them to the "Open in your player" screen and the pre-Shaka `/watch` live-transcode fallback is never offered; X-Men '97 (h264) plays. Decision in new `04-streaming-decision.md` (real-file probes + measured costs on this host, load-corrected): **option A** — keep Shaka/HLS, and for files the browser cannot decode at height < 2160 build an on-demand **cached H.264 compat package** (video re-encoded once, CRF21 veryfast; ~70-80 min wall + ~4.0-4.7 GB per 2h32m 1080p HEVC film ≈ 1.0× source; audio/subs per S14) that auto-falls back instead of the dead-end player screen; external-player flow stays. **B** (live `/watch` transcode only) rejected: per-play CPU on 8 real cores, no seeking, loses menus; **C** rejected: web player stays unable to play the common film tier. **4K capped-1080p rendition deferred** (>2.5 h CPU + ~4 GB/film, OOM-prone; 4K never played in-browser). No production code changed by the spike. |

# Default download to a web-exhibitable source instead of the most-seeded one

## Outcome / Problem

The one-click ("friendly") download picks the **most-seeded** matching source.
On real titles that source is often x265/HEVC (4K and/or 10-bit), which this
web app **cannot play in-browser** — those files land on the "Open in your
player" screen (`WatchPage.tsx:340-370`), and with the external-player setup
broken (T-001) the user is stuck with a download they can't watch from the app.

Real case: Batman and Blade Runner downloads are unplayable in the web player;
X-Men '97 (h264) plays fine. Root cause is the codec gate, not corruption:
`streamPlan.ts` returns `player-required` for HEVC ≥2160 and the `mseProbe`
short-circuits HEVC Main10/10-bit to the player screen (`hls.ts:336-342`,
`downloads.ts:218-222`). Chromium/Firefox on Linux have no HEVC decode path.

Goal: when auto-picking a source, prefer one the web app can actually exhibit —
falling back to most-seeded only when none qualifies — and make the behaviour a
Settings choice.

## User & impact

- Anyone using the friendly Download button on Detail pages (movies and per
  episode/season of TV).
- Fixes the "downloaded a big 4K x265 file I can't watch from the browser" trap;
  authors who want bit-perfect 4K can still get it via the Advanced picker.

## Context & Constraints

- Auto-pick helpers: `chooseEpisodePick` / `chooseSeasonPick` in
  `frontend/src/lib/coverage.ts`; invoked from `DetailPage.tsx:768,788`, where a
  caption already names the friendly pick next to the Download button
  (`DetailPage.tsx:89`). Sources are ordered by seeders before pick time.
- `Source` already carries the parsed hints needed to judge web-exhibitability:
  `resolution` (`2160p…`), `codec` (`x264|x265|AV1|…`), `hdr`, `isDolbyVision`
  (`frontend/src/types.ts:113-117`), produced by the release parser
  (`backend/src/lib/releaseParser.ts`). **No new parsing/probing required.**
- Browser-safe codecs in this app are h264/VP9/AV1 (`streamPlan.ts:8-9`);
  release tags only distinguish x264/x265/AV1. AV1 and x264 are safe; **x265 is
  never browser-safe here** (even 1080p 8-bit — no reliable HEVC decode on
  Linux Chromium/Firefox), and `hdr`/`isDolbyVision` almost always imply HEVC
  10-bit.
- Coverage semantics must survive the change: exact single-episode releases are
  preferred over partial packs, and whole-season packs are never auto-picked for
  an episode (`coverage.ts:40-48`).
- Existing Settings precedent: server-persisted (audio language) vs device
  localStorage (player choice). A download-pick preference is a per-user visual
  product setting; default to the **localStorage** pattern unless server
  persistence is requested.
- Author decision (analysis review): **source-picking fix only** — no transcode
  rendition work here; that belongs to the T-006 streaming analysis.

## Scope — In

- New Settings control: **Friendly download — pick by: `Most-seeded` (current,
  default) | `Web-playable first`**.
- When `Web-playable first`, the friendly pick ranks candidate sources by
  seeders **within the web-exhibitable subset** and only falls back to the
  overall most-seeded source when nothing qualifies. Applies to movies,
  per-episode, and season picks through the shared coverage helpers.
- Definition of web-exhibitable for the title heuristic:
  `codec ∈ {x264, AV1}`, `hdr === false`, `isDolbyVision === false`,
  `resolution !== '2160p'`. (Strict: unknown codec ⇒ not web-exhibitable.)
- The friendly-pick caption / chips surface the outcome ("Web-playable · x264
  1080p") so the user understands why a smaller/older source was chosen.

## Scope — Out

- Transcoding or "web-watch rendition" for HEVC/4K (T-006).
- Changing the Advanced picker or manual source table.
- Server-side/persistent settings table unless requested.
- Predicting actual container/bit-depth (only title hints are used).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Default behaviour unchanged: `Most-seeded` produces the same pick as today.
2. Setting `Web-playable first`: for a title whose most-seeded source is
   x265-2160p/HDR but that has any x264/AV1 ≤1080p SDR candidate, the friendly
   download picks the best-seeded web-exhibitable candidate and the UI caption
   says so.
3. Same title with only x265/4K candidates → falls back to most-seeded exactly
   as today (no pick is worse than today's, and no crash on empty).
4. Episode coverage rules hold in web-playable mode (exact-episode still beats
   partial pack; whole-season pack never auto-picked for an episode).
5. Choice persists across reloads and the Advanced picker is untouched.

## Approach / Locked decisions

- Locked: source-picking fix only (author), strict web-exhibitable definition,
  most-seeded as the default mode.
- Implementation sketch (owns details): add `webExhibitable(source): boolean`
  in `coverage.ts` (or `release.ts`), thread the current preference into
  `chooseEpisodePick`/`chooseSeasonPick` (or wrap them), and when web-playable
  mode is on reorder the candidate list to web-exhibitable-first while keeping
  per-group seeder ordering. Promote any behavior/decision changes to
  `docs/plan/` per repo rules.
- Known residual gap (accepted): a mis-tagged or codec-null release can still
  produce an unplayable download; this narrows the failure, does not eliminate
  it. Eliminating it entirely is the T-006 rendition path.

## Dependencies & Risks

- Depends on release-title tags being present and accurate (Prowlarr indexers
  with poor titles weaken the heuristic).
- HEVC support could someday land in browsers; re-check `SAFE_VIDEO_CODECS` and
  `hevcBeyondBrowserSupport` before ever treating x265 as web-exhibitable.
- T-001 remains the safety net for the files that still fall through to
  player-required.
