# On-demand cached H.264 compat package (auto-fallback for non-decodable ≤1080p files)

## Outcome / Problem

Spike **T-006** confirmed the root cause of "some downloads can't play in the web
player": The Dark Knight and Blade Runner 2049 here are **HEVC Main 10 / 10-bit at
1080p**, whose `playinfo.mseProbe` is `[]` (`hls.ts:307-342`), so the Watch MSE
preflight (`WatchPage.tsx:31-39,219-220`) sends them to the "Open in your player"
screen (`:340`) and the pre-Shaka `/watch` live-transcode fallback is never offered.
4K/UHD was `player-required` in both eras and stays that way (T-006 decision).

The T-006 decision (D22, `docs/plan/04-streaming-decision.md`): keep Shaka/HLS and,
for a completed file whose video the browser's MSE cannot decode with height **< 2160**,
build an **on-demand, cached H.264 "compat package"** (video re-encoded once) that the
player falls back to automatically — restoring the pre-Shaka universality for ≤1080p
HEVC (8-bit on Linux too) without the old per-play live-encode cost or seek loss. This
ticket implements it. Measured budget on this host (Ryzen 7 5700U, software ffmpeg):
~70-80 min wall + **≈4.0-4.7 GB** (`packages` volume) per 2h32m 1080p HEVC film
(≈1.0× source size), then cached — zero per replay.

## User & impact

- Anyone pressing Watch on a completed HEVC/x265 ≤1080p download that today lands on
  the dead-end player screen.
- Reduces the urgency of T-001 (external player) and T-003 (web-playable default)
  without removing them; the external-player + Download-file paths must keep working.

## Context & Constraints

- Packaging pipeline: `backend/src/lib/packages.ts` (`createPackageManager`, runs the
  S14 steps as concurrent ffmpeg processes with `-progress`), pure builders in
  `backend/src/lib/hls.ts` (`videoSegmentArgs` = `-c:v copy` today, `audioSegmentArgs`,
  `subtitleMediaPlaylist`, `buildMasterPlaylist`, `mseProbeTypes`),
  endpoints in `backend/src/routes/playback.ts` (`hls/status`, `hls/master.m3u8`,
  `DELETE /hls`, `pkg/:key/*`), package root `PACKAGE_DIR` on the `packages` volume,
  `DONE`-marker cache, deleted on torrent delete (S6). ffmpeg in the app image already
  software-decodes 10-bit HEVC (T-006 verified) — no image change.
- Frontend gating: `WatchPage.tsx` `canPlayHlsInBrowser`/`mseProbe` preflight
  (`:31-39`, `:146/178`), `isHls`/`needsPlayer` (`:219-220`), the player-required
  screen (`:340-371`) and package-status polling effect (`:222-257`). Shaka plays any
  single-rendition master; menus come from EXT-X-MEDIA groups.
- Browser reality (T-006): Linux Chrome/Firefox decode no HEVC at all, so the trigger
  must be the runtime `MediaSource.isTypeSupported` probe, not just bit depth/10-bit.
- Repo rules: API camelCase / DB snake_case; no production code decision without a
  `docs/plan/` entry (D22 already locks the approach; spec deltas S7b/S14 belong in
  `02-specs.md` and the D8/D22 wording in `00-index.md` when this lands).

## Scope — In

- **Backend**:
  - Let the package manager build a **compat variant** of a package: identical S14
    layout/master (`master.m3u8`, AUDIO/SUBTITLES groups, WebVTT subs) but the video
    rendition is re-encoded `libx264 -preset veryfast -crf 21 -pix_fmt yuv420p`
    (segment into 6 s fMP4 like `videoSegmentArgs`), audio per `canCopyAudioTrack` /
    AAC-192k, subs unchanged. Distinct cache key/`DONE` so the stream-copy and compat
    variants can coexist or replace cleanly; deletion on torrent delete covers both.
  - Expose it over the S14 endpoints (e.g. a `compat` variant on `hls/status` +
    `master.m3u8`, or a sibling route) so the existing progress UI is reused. A compat
    master must carry an h264 CODECS string (always MSE-decodable).
  - Keep the decision in `playinfo` honest: return what the file natively is AND that a
    compat variant is available for <2160 non-decodable video (extend S7b shape +
    `02-specs.md`), so the frontend does not guess.
- **Frontend** (`WatchPage.tsx`):
  - When the MSE preflight fails for a <2160 file, replace the dead-end player screen
    with a **"Building a web-compatible copy…"** state that starts the compat package
    (poll `status`, show progress + ETA like today's packaging), then plays the compat
    master through Shaka.
  - **Cancel to local player**: "Open in your player" (movie://, T-001) + Download file
    stay one click away from every state; never trap the user in an ~1 h build they
    didn't ask for (auto-start but always cancellable, and remember a "don't ask again
    for this file" choice).
- **Guardrails (locked by T-006)**:
  - At most **one** compat package build at a time; a compat build must not starve an
    active live `/watch` stream. The 2 s qBittorrent poll budget is unaffected.
  - `packages`-volume **eviction/size policy** for compat packages (≈1.0× source size
    each) — compat packages are the cheapest to rebuild (only the source is needed), so
    they are the first eviction candidates.
- **Docs**: update `02-specs.md` (S7b shape, S14 variant) and the D8/D22 wording if
  the behavioral contract changes.

## Scope — Out

- **4K (≥2160)**: stays `player-required` / external-player. The capped-1080p
  web rendition for 4K is deferred (T-006 decision: >2.5 h CPU + ~4 GB/film, OOM-prone,
  never worked in-browser anyway).
- Codec normalization / adding HEVC decode to browsers (none exists on Linux).
- DRM / adaptive multi-bitrate renditions (single rendition only).
- Changing the good path (h264/vp9/av1 direct/HLS, AAC stream-copy, menus).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The Dark Knight + Blade Runner 2049 (the real 1080p HEVC Main 10 downloads) **play
   in-browser** via a built-on-demand H.264 compat package with working seek, and their
   audio/subtitle menus work; second watch of the same file starts without rebuilding.
2. X-Men '97 (h264) still plays through the existing stream-copy path and is **not**
   re-encoded (no compat build when the browser can decode the file natively).
3. A 4K HEVC download still routes to the player screen (no capped rendition, no compat
   build attempted).
4. The player screen for a non-decodable <2160 file is replaced by the building state
   with live progress and a working **Open in your player** / Download-file cancel path;
   after cancel, re-entering Watch offers the choice again without rebuilding from 0
   unless the user asks (failed/stale package cleared via existing `DELETE /hls` retry).
5. Only one compat package build runs at a time (a second request reports packaging
   progress, not a second ffmpeg); the 2 s poll keeps firing on time.
6. Deleting the torrent removes its compat package from the `packages` volume (same as
   S6 today).
7. Tests: `packages.test.ts`/`hls.test.ts` unit coverage for the compat variant layout
   + CODECS, `playinfo`/endpoint tests, and `WatchPage.test.tsx` for the new state
   machine (build → play, cancel, failure → retry). Typecheck/lint/test + frontend
   build green.
8. Spec docs updated (S7b/S14/D22) in the same change.

## Approach / Locked decisions

- Locked by T-006 (D22): **Strategy A** — keep Shaka, add the cached H.264 compat
  package with auto-fallback; trigger = browser MSE cannot decode the file's video AND
  height < 2160; 4K capped rendition deferred; external-player flow retained; one build
  at a time + never starving a live stream.
- Implementation sketch (owns details): thread a `compat?: boolean` through the package
  key + `runPackage` video step (choose `videoSegmentArgs` vs the measured libx264
  args) and through the S14 endpoints/playinfo; reuse the existing status/progress and
  DONE caching. Encode profile is the existing repo-wide transcode profile
  (`veryfast crf 21 yuv420p`, `transcode.ts`) — do not invent a new one. Record the
  packages-volume eviction policy in `docs/plan/` when chosen (decision, not code).

## Dependencies & Risks

- Depends on T-006's decision doc (`docs/plan/04-streaming-decision.md`, D22) — the
  authoritative source for rationale and measured costs; read it first.
- Risk: an ~1 h first-watch build is a UX surprise — mitigations are the always-on
  progress + cancel-to-local-player and the remembered per-file choice. Risk: disk
  growth from ≈1.0×-source packages — eviction policy (In scope) addresses it.
- T-001/T-003 remain the safety nets; this shrinks but does not remove their urgency.
- When this lands, the D22/`04-streaming-decision.md` "consequence" section becomes the
  verification checklist.

1: # T-006 — Web-streaming decision (spike output)
2: 
3: Date: 2026-09-07. Status: **approved by spike (T-006)**. Implementation lives in the
4: follow-up ticket T-007. This document records the spike's verification and costing,
5: compares the candidate strategies, and states the decision. No production code was
6: changed by the spike itself.
7: 
8: ## 1. Problem restated
9: 
10: Some fully-downloaded movies cannot be watched in the in-browser player. Real cases in
11: this install: **The Dark Knight ("Batman")** and **Blade Runner 2049** are unplayable;
12: **X-Men '97** plays fine. The author remembered that "before [the Shaka player],
13: ffmpeg-based playback seemed to play more video types", and asked whether Shaka is the
14: right choice and whether it is well configured.
15: 
16: The spike verified the root-cause hypothesis on the real files, measured the CPU/disk
17: cost of the candidate strategies on this host, and picked one.
18: 
19: ## 2. Real-file verification (acceptance criterion 1)
20: 
21: All three problem files were probed with the app's own pipeline: `ffprobe` full
22: stream dump (identical args to `lib/mediaInfo.ts`) plus the live `playinfo` response
23: (`S7b`) from the running backend, and the frontend gating decision was traced in code.
24: 
25: | File (download row) | ffprobe video | audio / subs | `playinfo` mode | `mseProbe` | In-browser result |

### B. Drop Shaka; route everything through live `/watch` ffmpeg (the old behavior)

- **CPU**: identical encoder, but **per play** — every watch of a 2h32m HEVC film
  burns ~50-90 min of box CPU at ~1.7-2.9× realtime headroom. Two concurrent watches

- **Seek**: none for transcoded files (progressive pipe, restart-to-seek) — a

  `/watch` stream or the 2 s qBittorrent poll (poll CPU is negligible either way).
- Disk: eviction/size policy for the `packages` volume (compat packages are ~1.0× the
  source's size).
- 4K (>2160p or 2160p non-decodable): unchanged, stays on the external-player flow.
- External-player + Download-file stay reachable from every Watch state.

## 6. What was NOT changed

No production code (backend or frontend) was modified by this spike. Benchmark artifacts
lived in the backend container's `/tmp` and were removed.

## What changed (spike — no production code)

**Committed (2 commits on `ticket/T-006`, working tree clean):**

## Acceptance-criteria verification

1. **Real-file verification (confirmed, recorded in the doc §2).** Probed the actual downloads with the app's own ffprobe args + live `playinfo` from the running stack: The Dark Knight ("Batman") and Blade Runner 2049 are **HEVC Main 10 / yuv420p10le 1080p** → `mseProbe: []`; X-Men '97 is h264/High → plays. Code-gated exactly as hypothesized (`hls.ts:307-342`, `WatchPage.tsx:31-39, 219-220, 340`); pre-Shaka `/watch` transcode handled sub-2160 HEVC, 4K was `player-required` in both eras.
2. **Decision doc compares A/B/C with explicit CPU/disk/seek/latency/quality tradeoffs** and picks **A** (keep Shaka + cached on-demand H.264 "compat package" for non-decodable <2160 video), rationale tied to the repo's constraints (single-user self-host, 8 real cores, ffmpeg already in the image and able to software-decode 10-bit HEVC, existing `PACKAGE_DIR`/S14 pipeline, 2 s poll unaffected). **4K capped-1080p rendition deferred** with measured rationale.
3. **Follow-up ticket filed** as above.
4. **No production code changed by T-006** — diff vs the base commit is docs-only; T-006 closed.

## Costing was measured, not guessed (doc §3)

On this host (Ryzen 7 5700U, app's own Alpine-ffmpeg 8.0.1 container): 1080p HEVC-Main10 → H.264 `veryfast crf 21` runs **≈1.7× realtime (load≈30) to ≈2.9× (load≈19)**; a full-file fMP4 package build sustained ≈2.2× → **≈70 min wall** for the 2h32m film at **≈4.0–4.7 GB** (≈1.0× source) on the `packages` volume. 2160p→1080p scaled encode ≈0.9× realtime → **>2.5 h + OOM risk at low RAM** (a 4K decode OOM-killed at ~2 GB free), which justifies deferring the 4K rendition. Benchmark artifacts were removed; the app's `/api/health` + playinfo were re-checked green afterward.

## Checks

`npm run typecheck/lint/test` and the frontend build were **not run — nothing to flag**: no package source changed (commit diff touches only `docs/plan/*`), and neither package has `node_modules` in this fresh worktree, so a suite run would test byte-identical code. Docs-only change; no markdown linter exists in the repo.

One environment side-note: the spike's killed benchmark processes left three inert `<defunct>` ffmpeg children (PPID 1) in the running `movie-downloader-backend-1` container; they consume nothing and only a container restart reaps them — I did not restart the user's live stack to avoid disrupting other work.
